description: Diagnostic-only run, 2026-08-04, used to confirm the root cause of the 0.31% bug before fixing it. layer1_description.txt's few-shot 'Examples:' block was stripped in-memory only (the real file on disk was never modified for this test) and layer 1 was called alone via render_prompt()+call_ollama() on the same real input as 01-model-input.json.
anomaly_description: The diagnostic system has detected a medium-risk anomaly affecting the cooling system. Specifically, two key signals are outside their normal ranges: the coolant temperature is elevated at 98.0°C (above the expected 90.0-95.0°C), and the mass airflow sensor integral over 180 seconds exceeds its limit at 3000.0g (where it should be below 2500.0g). These abnormal readings suggest that the cooling system may not be functioning optimally, potentially due to issues such as a thermostat stuck closed or insufficient coolant flow. The risk level is classified as medium, indicating that while there is no immediate danger, this condition should be monitored and addressed soon to prevent further degradation. The model projects a 100% probability of crossing the high-risk threshold within the next 10 trips, with an estimated four drive cycles remaining until failure if the issue persists.
finding: Removing the examples entirely fixed the 0.31% leak (correct 100%/4 cycles appeared), but introduced two regressions: (1) tone became clinical ('The diagnostic system has detected...' instead of 'Your vehicle's cooling system...'), and (2) 'until failure' overclaims closer to a confirmed outcome than the prompt's own rules allow (see layer1_description.txt lines 84-85). This is why the final fix kept the examples and added explicit anti-leakage guardrail text instead of deleting them — see 05-rag-llm-output-after-fix.json for the result of that approach.
